confirmed.title: Sift's bar Search button no longer sends the field's change and blur before clicking the page's button, so a search without a form runs with the old query
confirmed.where: src/content/index.ts:774 (mousedown on 'form.search button[type=submit]' is cancelled, F856) with src/content/proxy.ts:598 (no-form search with via 'button': click(button) without finishEditing)
confirmed.evidence: Fixture fx/r9int-searchchange.html is a bar search with no <form>. Its query is kept on the field's change event, as a value binding does, and its Search button reads it. Mouse: type 'bread' in Sift's bar field, click Sift's Search. Current build: page log ['search ""'], results 'Type something to search.'. Original (Sift off, same mouse flow): ['change bread','blur','search "bread"'], 'Results for bread…'. Pre-round-8 build (sift-r8-base on port 9477): ['change bread','blur','search "bread"'], same results as the original. Before, mousedown moved focus off Sift's field, so H.leave sent change and blur first. Now focus stays, and proxy.submit's no-form button path only clicks the page button.
confirmed.repro: Start the test Chrome. Run SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r9int/searchchange.ts. It prints SIFT {"log":["search \"\""]…}. Add 'orig' as the first argument for the original. By hand: open http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r9int-searchchange.html, type 'bread' in Sift's top search field, and click Sift's Search button with the mouse.
confirmed.suspectedCause: F856 keeps focus in the field to stop Discourse's blur, but the field's edit then never ends. In proxy.submit's no-form branch, finishEditing(field) (change) should run before click(button), as the blur did before.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice on the current build (port 9467) with fx/r9int-searchchange.html. I typed 'bread' in Sift's bar field and clicked Sift's Search with the mouse. Page log: ['search ""'], results 'Type something to search.' Original (Sift off, same mouse flow): ['change bread','blur','search "bread"'] and 'Results for bread…'. The pre-round-8 build (scratchpad/pre8, which is sift-r8-base's src, on 9477) gave the same as the original in 2 of 2 runs, so this is a regression. In the code, index.ts ~774 cancels mousedown on 'form.search button[type=submit]' while focus is in that form's field (F856), so focus never leaves the field and H.leave never sends change and blur. proxy.submit's no-form branch with via 'button' then runs only `else if (button) click(button)`, with no finishEditing. The form branch and the Enter branch both call finishEditing, so only the mouse button path on searches without a form is hit. That limits the scope to pages that commit the query on change or blur (Knockout value bindings, v-model.lazy). On those pages it is a real wrong-result search. I would call it medium to high.
confirmed.fix: src/content/proxy.ts submit(), no-form branch: call finishEditing(field) before click(button) when field is set (`else if (button) { if (field) finishEditing(field); click(button); }`). Or in index.ts H.submit, flush the field's change (and a blur if wanted) before proxy.submit when F856's mousedown kept focus in the field.

confirmed.where: src/content/index.ts:995-1005 (escapeList: hidden(true) dismisses the list even when the page still shows it) and src/content/index.ts:3185-3190 (only H.input on the same field clears that dismissal)

Current build: the click shows Sift's sheet with 27-31. After Escape, the sheet is gone while the page calendar is still open. Tab goes to 'Book'. Shift+Tab back, a click on the field, and ArrowDown all leave the sheet 'none'. The field is read-only, so no typing can bring it back, and the day cannot be picked in Sift. confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice on the current build with fx/r9int-pickesc.html. Clicking the read-only Day field shows Sift's sheet with 27-31. After Escape the sheet is 'none' while the page calendar stays open. Tab goes to 'Book'. Shift+Tab back, another click on the field, and ArrowDown all leave the sheet 'none'. In an extra run I clicked Sift's heading and then the field again, and still nothing came back after 7 s: the page calendar never closes (Sift's own presses do not reach the page's outside-mousedown handler), so the dismissal is never lifted. In the code, escapeList's `setTimeout(() => hidden(true), 0)` (index.ts ~995-1005, the F853 change) forces the dismissal for any list the page still shows. Pre8's hidden() returned early whenever the list was still visible. This is a regression, but only for pickers that ignore Escape. jQuery UI and Bootstrap pickers close on Escape, so they are not affected. Medium to high.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts escapeList: force the dismissal (hidden(true)) only for plain-search panels (fieldPanel 'fp:' / fieldList 'fl:' keys, the F853 case). And/or in H.focus and H.fieldClick, when escapedList?.ref === ref, delete escapedList.key from store.dismissed and dismissedRefs, as H.input already does, so pressing the field again brings the page's still-open popup back.

confirmed.title: After a message is sent, the page's fresh message field gets the sent text again, and a second Enter sends it twice
confirmed.where: src/content/index.ts:3082 (sift-focus listener calls liveField(refOf(pageFocus)) with sync on) and src/content/index.ts:2864 (proxy.setValue(now, mine.value))
confirmed.evidence: Fixture fx/r9int-resend.html is a chat form. On submit it posts the text, replaces the input name=message with a fresh empty one in the same place, and focuses it, as a keyed composer or an HTMX swap with autofocus does. Sift: type 'hello team', press Enter. Sent ['hello team'], but the page field and Sift's field both hold 'hello team'. A second Enter gives sent ['hello team','hello team']. Original: after Enter the page field is '' and the second Enter sends nothing. A page-side trace shows change@old, then focus@new and input@new='hello team' within 9 ms. That is liveField adopting the fresh field on the page's focus() and copying Sift's stale text into it. The pre-round-8 build does the same.
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r9int/resend.ts. Add 'orig' as the first argument for the original. resend2.ts in the same folder prints the event trace.
confirmed.suspectedCause: liveField's sync copies Sift's field value into the adopted field even right after an action. carry() already guards this with lastTyped > store.actAt, and the sift-focus path should use the same guard (or sync=false).
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice on the current build with fx/r9int-resend.html. I typed 'hello team' and pressed Enter. Result: sent ['hello team'], but the page's fresh field and Sift's field both hold 'hello team'. A second Enter gives sent ['hello team','hello team']. Original: after Enter the page field is '' and the second Enter sends nothing. The pre-round-8 build does the same as the current one, so this is not a regression. In the code, the 'sift-focus' listener (index.ts ~3082) calls liveField(refOf(pageFocus)) with the default sync=true when the page focuses the field it swapped in. liveField then runs proxy.setValue(now, mine.value) (~2864), which copies Sift's stale text into the page's new empty field. carry() has a lastTyped > store.actAt guard against exactly this, and this path does not. It only hits pages that replace the composer element after a send and focus the new one (keyed remount, HTMX outerHTML with autofocus). When it does, it leads to duplicate sends or old text stuck in the field. High is fair.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts sift-focus listener: call liveField(refOf(pageFocus), false) there, or in liveField only sync when lastTyped(mine) > store.actAt, the same guard carry() uses. Then Sift's field takes the page's new (empty) value on the next render.

confirmed.title: When the page redraws the cart row being edited, Sift moves focus to the first field with the same label, so the next key changes another item's quantity
confirmed.where: src/content/index.ts:302-303 (twinOf falls back to the first control with the same label), used by refocusNow at src/content/index.ts:352-353. The page's own focus on the redrawn field is ignored at src/content/index.ts:3088 because no action was recent.
confirmed.evidence: Fixture fx/r9int-cartrow.html has 3 rows, each labelled 'Quantity' with name=qty, as in Shopify's Dawn cart. After a quantity is saved, the page redraws that row and focuses its new field. In Sift: click the 2nd Quantity (Seeded rye), type '1', wait 1.5 s, type '2'. Result: rows [row-a:21, row-b:11, row-c:1], log ['b=11','a=21'], and focus ends on Rye loaf's Quantity. Original: [row-a:1, row-b:211, row-c:1], log ['b=11','b=211']: only Seeded rye changes. With per-item labels (?v=named), Sift matches the original. The pre-round-8 build is worse ('a=11','a=211'). Round 8 removed the text carry (F851) but kept the label-only focus.
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r9int/cartrow.ts. Add 'orig' as the first argument for the original, or append '?v=named' as the second argument for the control.
confirmed.suspectedCause: With several Sift controls sharing the label, twinOf takes the first. It should prefer the same rank among same-label controls, or follow the page's own focus() into the redrawn same-kind field while the user is typing (allow pageFocusTo when typedAt is recent).
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice on the current build with fx/r9int-cartrow.html. I clicked the 2nd 'Quantity' (Seeded rye), typed '1', waited 1.5 s, then typed '2'. Result: rows [row-a:21, row-b:11, row-c:1], log ['b=11','a=21'], and Sift's focus ends on Rye loaf's Quantity (value 21). Original: [row-a:1, row-b:211, row-c:1], log ['b=11','b=211']. With ?v=named (per-item labels), Sift matches the original. The pre-round-8 build is worse: ['b=11','a=11','a=211']. Not a regression. The cause is in index.ts. liveField cannot adopt the redrawn field: the nearest connected container (#rows) holds 3 qty fields, so `place.n[i] !== 1 && i > 0` returns null. The page's own focus() on the new field is ignored because no action was recent (the check at ~3088). refocusNow then calls twinOf, which falls back to `all.find(c => labelOf(c) === spot.label)`, the first 'Quantity'. Dawn-style carts label every row 'Quantity' and refocus the redrawn row, so the next key or ArrowUp changes the wrong item's quantity. High.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts: record in spotOf the spot's rank among Sift controls with the same tag and label, and in twinOf pick the same-label control at that rank (fall back to the first only when there is a single one). Or, in the sift-focus listener, follow the page's focus() into a same-kind field when typedAt is recent (treat recent typing like a recent action), so focus goes to Sift's copy of the field the page focused.

confirmed.where: src/content/index.ts:1768-1776 (wakeEmbeds: el.scrollIntoView on the hidden original, up to 3 s per embed)

Below the article, an IntersectionObserver (rootMargin 800px) loads the next story. Current build: about 1.7 s after load the page log shows 'first scroll' and 'next story loaded'. Sift's main view then contains the next story's text ('coastal road'), and the reader never scrolled there. Pre-round-8 build: log [], no next story. On La Nación (F830's URL) the original was scrolled to y=2882 twice, at 6.4 s and 19.4 s, each time for about 6 s.
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r9int/nextart.ts prints log ['first scroll…','next story loaded…']. Then bun scripts/act.ts "eval:document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelector('#sift-main').textContent.includes('coastal road')" prints true. With the pre-round-8 build (port 9477), the log is [].
confirmed.suspectedCause: scrollIntoView({block:'center'}) shows the whole viewport around the embed in the original, so any scroll-linked loader near it fires too. Bring only the embed into view (block 'nearest' near the viewport's top edge), or skip waking when the scroll would reach the page's end.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice on the current build with fx/r9int-nextart.html. About 1.7 s after load the page log shows ['first scroll at ~1700','next story loaded at ~1700']. Sift's #sift-main then contains the next story's text ('coastal road' is true; its paragraphs are appended at the end of Sift's view), though the reader never got near the end. The original's scroll is restored afterward (docY 0). The pre-round-8 build: log [] and 'coastal road' false, so this is a regression from the F830 change. In the code, wakeEmbeds (index.ts ~1751-1777) calls el.scrollIntoView({block:'center'}) on the hidden original for each embed quote and holds it there up to 3 s. Any scroll-linked loader near the embed fires (next-story loaders, lazy comments, read tracking). I did not check La Nación live; the evidence is the fixture plus the code. One caution on the reporter's fix: block 'nearest' or 'start' would not help here, because with an 800 px rootMargin the sentinel right after the embed still intersects. Medium is fair.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts wakeEmbeds: skip (or defer until the reader scrolls near it in Sift) any embed whose wake scroll would bring the viewport within about a screen plus a margin of the document's end (el's bottom + scrollY + innerHeight + ~1000 > scrollHeight). Or watch for large content appended outside the embed during the wake, and stop waking when that happens. Changing only the scrollIntoView block option is not enough.

Reproduced twice with the given eval: [9,6] on load, then [25,19] after '+ Show All 19 Incidents'. The claim is wrong on one point: the incidents are not dropped. They are folded. Sift's shadow DOM has

August 2026

After October is expanded, both 'September 2026' and 'August 2026' become collapsed sections. The original shows all three previews of every month in plain view. Cause, from the code: the incident bodies are div.message with text between

and no

. So the F832 fallback in findArticle() (src/content/extract/generic.ts, about line 3203, 'No story in

s: one set as runs of text between
s') picks one long incident body as the page's article. That is why 'Incident across several services' (and, after expanding, the Oct 5 'Incident with Actions') gets 'Show full text'. article() then sets ctx.afterArticle = true, and itemsInto() (about line 4704) folds every later list as 'more stories after the article', titled by the month H2. In src/content/extract/generic.ts findArticle(), in the F832

confirmed.title: Cloudflare bot-check page: Sift hides the 'Verify you are human' checkbox, so a person in Sift cannot pass the check
confirmed.evidence: One load of Stack Overflow got Cloudflare's 'Performing security verification' page. Sift showed only 'stackoverflow.com', the H2 'Performing security verification' and the paragraph about bots: no checkbox, no hint, nothing to act on (/home/nico/projects/sift-test-4/research/shots/r9t4-so-trending.png). With Sift switched off, the same page shows the Turnstile widget 'Verify you are human' with its checkbox (/home/nico/projects/sift-test-4/research/shots/r9t4-so-cf-orig.png). The page's light DOM has no iframe, only a 0x0 input, so the widget seems to sit in a closed shadow root that Sift's challenges.cloudflare/turnstile portal rule cannot see. I did not click or otherwise interact with the check. A later load passed on its own.
confirmed.repro: When stackoverflow.com (or any Cloudflare site) answers with 'Performing security verification': SIFT_PORT=9464 SIFT_TAB=T4-generic bun scripts/act.ts shot:cf-sift press:Alt+Shift+S wait:1500 shot:cf-orig press:Alt+Shift+S. cf-sift has no checkbox, and cf-orig shows 'Verify you are human'. Do not click the checkbox.
confirmed.suspectedCause: Unverified. extract/generic.ts portals Turnstile only when it finds an iframe from challenges.cloudflare.com. On the new challenge page the widget is in a closed shadow root, so nothing is portaled. A challenge page (title 'Just a moment...', a cf-turnstile-response input) could show the original instead, or portal the widget's host element.
confirmed.verdict: Stack Overflow was not challenged in my run. I reproduced the same Sift behavior on two other Cloudflare challenge pages, without clicking anything. On https://www.timeanddate.com/ (title 'Just a moment...', input[name=cf-turnstile-response] present), Sift's outline is only 'H1 Just a moment…' and 'p: Nothing to show yet.' (research/shots/skeptic-cf-sift.png). With Sift off, the original shows the 'Verify you are human' checkbox widget (research/shots/skeptic-cf-orig.png). It was the same on https://www.allrecipes.com/: Sift shows 'Just a moment... / Nothing to show yet.', and the original shows the checkbox widget (research/shots/skeptic-cf-orig2.png). Both pages have 0 iframes in the light DOM. The widget is a 650x69 (or 300x72) div whose only light children are div > input#cf-chl-widget-…_response (0x0), so the frame sits in a closed shadow root. The iframe-src rules (EMBED_HOST/TOOL_HOST 'challenges.cloudflare|turnstile') never match. A person in Sift gets a dead page with no control and no hint. They must find the switch to pass the check. The behavior is Sift's, not the site's, and no bot check is worked around. Not a regression: research/site-sweep.md already recorded 'Just a moment... / Nothing to show yet.' on Allrecipes.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts (the portal and embed detection that uses EMBED_HOST/TOOL_HOST), treat a Cloudflare challenge widget as a tool portal: the host element of input[name=cf-turnstile-response] or [id^=cf-chl-widget] (its sized ancestor), even when no iframe is visible. Or detect a challenge page (that input plus a title like 'Just a moment...' or 'Performing security verification') in src/content/index.ts and show the original page, or a notice with a 'Show original to verify' action, instead of 'Nothing to show yet.'

confirmed.title: GOV.UK passport renewal guide shows a 14-year-old date ('Oct 10, 2012') under the H1 that the page never shows
confirmed.evidence:
Sift's outline: 'H1 Renew or replace your adult passport' and then 'p: Oct 10, 2012' (

). The original's text has no '2012' anywhere. The date comes from the page's JSON-LD ("datePublished": "2012-10-10T20:37:20+01:00"; dateModified 2015-01-12; meta govuk:updated-at 2026-09-09). The page has no meta article date and no . A reader is told this passport guide dates from 2012 when it was updated in 2026. The round 8 F832 change added ldDate() as the byline date fallback (diff around line 1497, '+ if (!when) when = ldDate();'), so this is new with the merge. I did not run the old build. /council-tax and /pay-council-tax show no date. Outline /home/nico/projects/sift-test-4/research/shots/r9t4-govoverview.txt
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9464 SIFT_TAB=T4-generic bun scripts/act.ts goto:https://www.gov.uk/renew-adult-passport/renew wait:5000 'eval:[document.querySelector("sift-root").shadowRoot.querySelector("main h1 + p")?.innerText, /2012/.test(document.body.innerText)]' prints ['Oct 10, 2012', false].
confirmed.suspectedCause: src/content/extract/generic.ts byline(): the new ldDate() fallback takes the first datePublished of any *Article in JSON-LD. GOV.UK guides use an Article schema with the first-publish date. The fallback could require that the visible page shows a date, or prefer dateModified, or apply only to news articles.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on both URLs. On /renew-adult-passport/renew and /renew-adult-passport, the eval prints ['Oct 10, 2012', false]: Sift's p after the H1 says 'Oct 10, 2012', and '2012' appears nowhere in the original's text. The page has no <time>. Its JSON-LD has @type 'Article' with datePublished 2012-10-10T20:37:20+01:00 and dateModified 2015-01-12, while meta govuk:updated-at is 2026-09-09. In the code, byline() (src/content/extract/generic.ts, about line 6645) falls back to ldDate() ('TOI has no meta date and no <time>, F832'). ldDate() (about line 6575) accepts any @type ending in 'Article' and returns its datePublished. GOV.UK's plain 'Article' schema carries the 2012 first-publish date. Sift shows it with no label, as if it were the guide's date, on official guidance updated in 2026. The likely result is that every GOV.UK guide shows its 2012-2015 first-publish date. Medium: it misleads the reader about how current the guidance is.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts ldDate(), accept only news and blog types (/(NewsArticle|ReportageNewsArticle|AnalysisNewsArticle|BlogPosting|LiveBlogPosting)$/) rather than any '*Article'. Also, or instead, use the JSON-LD date only when its year (or the formatted date) appears in the page's visible text. Prefer dateModified, or a meta '*updated-at', when it is newer.

skeptic.verdict: Checked on 2 loads of https://www.booking.com/ with identical outlines. The F858 problem is fixed. Sift's main starts with 'H1 Booking.com' and then the dates and travelers controls. 'No purchase necessary', '$5,000 Cruise Giveaway' and 'Enter here' do not appear in Sift. The original's body still has 'Giveaway' and 'No purchase necessary'. The tester is right that the 'Offers' block still shows 'H3 Earn 6% in Travel Credits on stays with the Genius Rewards Visa®', its terms line and 'Learn more' (data-testid='promotional-banner-content-title' on the original). But it sits far down, under the site's own heading 'Offers / Promotions, deals, and special offers for you', after the search form and the 'Why Booking.com?' block. It no longer takes the H1 or the first screen, which is what made F858 medium. Alone it is a low-severity leftover. I would count F858 as fixed, and if wanted, file the Visa card as a separate low finding: add data-testid*='promotional-banner' or 'Rewards Visa'/credit-card wording to promo detection in src/content/extract/generic.ts.
